page.layout: One printed page. Running head at top with page number 120 left and title "Roma Irreconciliabilis" right. One text column in the centre. Left margin holds one marginal note "Socr.l.5.c.21." and some faint, mostly illegible marginal notes further down. Below the text block a catchword-like line "iftuc" with "moda" at the right, which is the catchword of the following page.

main_text.p: istuc accenseri solent: Insigni-tè sit improbus oportet, qui istanc licentiam non perhor-rescat. De istis vaticinatum puto Socratem historicum dum ait ; Nonnulli scortatio-nem rem quidem indifferen-tem arbitrantur, sed tamen de diebus festis tanquam de vita decertant. Mitto quæ Socr.l.5.c.21. ... (vt appellat Chryso-stomus) nomine,re,condicio-ne,ac pœna,vtrinque non leui verborum lite, (vt Cassandro visum) disceptari solent. Nec attingo Euangelicam voto-rum perfectionem, nec peri-culosissimam temerè vouenti-um seruitutem, nec incom-moda
main_text.notes: The Greek phrases after "quæ" (rendered as a placeholder here) are printed in Greek letters and could not be read reliably. The faint marginal notes in the left margin below the Socr. note are too blurred to transcribe. The catchword "moda" is at the foot right; the left foot shows "istuc" which is the start of the following page's text.
